単.meaning: A knight's <part>armor</part> has a hundred buckles, and getting dressed takes all morning. One day a spark from the <part>fireworks</part> lands on it, and he throws the whole lot off. Now he wears one plain shirt with a hole for his head. Much more <kanji>simple</kanji>.
単.on: He strolls home through the dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, light as a feather.
単.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' he giggles, swinging round a <sound>to</sound>tem pole in his thin shirt. '<sound>Eh</sound>? Cold!' Just a single layer.

簡.meaning: A monk builds his home from four <part>bamboo</part> poles and leaves a wide <part>interval</part> between two of them for a door. No furniture, no clutter, just sunlight falling through the gap. He loves its <kanji>simplicity</kanji>.
簡.on: The only decoration is one pink <sound>car</sound>nation in a cup.
簡.kun: An <sound>e</sound>lephant offers him a sofa, but he shakes his head, picks a single stick to sit on and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': he chooses.

川.meaning: Three long lines run down the hillside side by side, like ribbons dropped from a giant's pocket. A paper boat is set down at the top and swirls along them all the way to the sea. You're looking at a <kanji>river</kanji>.
川.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try on the bridge salutes every paper boat that floats by.
川.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps at the boat, and the mouse sailing it yells '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

流.meaning: A lazy <part>squid</part> lets go of its rock and stretches out its trailing arms. The rushing <part>water drops</part> carry it along, past fish and boats, without one flick of its fins. It just rides the <kanji>current</kanji>.
流.on: At the river mouth it bumps into all its cousins: a squid <sound>reu</sound>nion!
流.kun: A <sound>na</sound>an stuffed with <sound>gar</sound>lic drifts past, and they all float after it.

鍵.meaning: A dragon sleeps on a mountain of <part>gold</part>, but it worries about thieves. So it melts one coin and sets out to <part>build</part> a tiny thing with teeth along one edge. Now only that fits the cave door: it's the <kanji>key</kanji>.
鍵.on: The dragon hides it in its pet's <sound>ken</sound>nel, where no thief would look.
鍵.kun: But a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the moat and a flock of <sound>gee</sound>se saw everything.

復.meaning: A broken <part>deck chair</part> rides the <part>chairlift</part> up to the carpenter at the top of the mountain. She glues its legs, paints it bright yellow and sends it back down as good as new. She can <kanji>restore</kanji> anything.
復.on: At the bottom it's hung back on its <sound>hoo</sound>k by the pool.
復.kun: A lla<sound>ma</sound> sits on it and snaps it, then offers a <sound>ta</sound>co to say sorry. Up the lift it goes again.

往.meaning: A <part>lord</part> refuses to walk anywhere, so a <part>chairlift</part> is strung from his castle over the hills. He rides it for days with a picnic on his lap, waving to the sheep below. It's his grand <kanji>journey</kanji>.
往.on: He stops for the night in the branches of a giant <sound>oa</sound>k.
往.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' he squeals at every bump, but on he goes.
